summary: Reviewed SessionComicsFilterTest.php (6 integration tests) and the supporting FilterSettingsTests.php (8 unit tests, WP-001). Inspected SessionComicsFilter, ComicsFilter, User, UserCollection, Session, MockUserCollection, and WebcomicsBuilderTestCase source files.

All 6 acceptance criteria are met. 98/98 PHPUnit tests pass (1 pre-existing skip). PHPStan level 5 is clean. Code follows all project conventions: strict_types, final test class, classmap autoloading, JSON-only persistence.

Singleton injection via ReflectionProperty is a well-established workaround given the current architecture. setUp/tearDown properly isolate state (singleton reset + $_SESSION = []). ReflectionProperty is initialized once in setUpBeforeClass to avoid per-test overhead.
No blocking issues found. Three low-priority non-blocking observations recorded.

metrics.test_coverage: 6 new integration tests in SessionComicsFilterTest.php + 8 unit tests in FilterSettingsTests.php; all 6 ACs covered

comments.note: SessionComicsFilter uses direct static calls to Session::getUser() and UserCollection::create() in its constructor. This forces test code to reach into the UserCollection singleton via ReflectionProperty. Adding a protected resolveUser(): ?User hook method would eliminate the reflection workaround entirely without changing the external contract. This is the single highest-leverage structural change that would improve testability.

SessionComicsFilter constructor silently writes back to the session (Session::set('comicsFilter', $resolved->getData())) when user filterSettings are loaded. This is an observable side-effect on construction that is not documented in a comment. A one-line comment explaining the intent (keeping session and user filters in sync on load) would prevent future surprises.

ComicsFilter::reset() does not reset orderBy or orderDir to their default values. importValues() therefore preserves prior orderBy/orderDir when called with an empty orderBy string (the guard in_array fails for orderDir and the idExists guard prevents an unknown orderBy). The behavior is consistent and tests pass, but the asymmetry between reset() zeroing status/searchText and silently retaining orderBy/orderDir is non-obvious. A brief comment on ComicsFilter::reset() clarifying the intent would help future maintainers.
